name: How is crown molding attached to kitchen cabinets?

mainEntity.name: How is crown molding attached to kitchen cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kitchen crown molding is mounted either directly to the cabinet face frame or to an added nailer board along the top. If upper cabinets do not run entirely to the ceiling, installers attach a standard crown molding or decorative riser board. When cabinets reach the ceiling, a two-piece system featuring an adjustable riser board and crown profile is often used. This two-piece assembly allows the installer to absorb uneven drywall or ceiling dips without leaving visible gaps or throwing the molding off-level.
acceptedAnswer.description: Crown molding attaches to cabinet face frames or added backing boards, often using a two-piece system with a riser board if extending seamlessly to the ceiling.
